newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond futures burst ahead once again.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond futures burst ahead once again.

text.p: *Australian bond futures edged to fresh 1-1/2 month highs in early trading after a set back in after hours trading on a fall in U.S. Treasuries proved short lived.
*U.S. sees further data suggesting a Fed rate hike in May.
Australian bond futures saw a burst of activity once again at the start of trading, edging to fresh 1-1/2 month highs after a set back in SYCOM on a fall in U.S. Treasuries proved short lived.
Traders said the amount of volume going through in the first 30 minutes of trading suggested U.S. hedge funds were again in the market with little physical activity seen as yet.
"There's resistance at 92.200/91.210 on the 10-year contract which could contain the market, but the way it has behaved recently it's definitely not a certainty," one trader said.
The June 10-year bond futures contract touched a high of 92.210 just after the opening, bringing the current rally to nearly 30 basis points since Monday's low.

Expectations of a market friendly outcome at next Wednesday's CPI report and hopes that wages growth will remain contained has resulted in a strong bid this week, following through the rally seen after last week's weak labour force data.

Bill futures remain firm and the June contract at a high of 94.06 equates to a cash rate of 5.94 percent, just below current 6.0 percent official rates, while further forward postions continue to push thoughts of a rate hike out to next year.
In contrast, the U.S. markets saw further data suggesting that the Federal Open Market Committee will endorse another tightening in the Fed funds rate when it meets on May 20.
A stronger than expected 0.9 percent rise in March industrial production and a rise to 84.1 percent in capacity utilisation overshadowed a 6.4 percent decline in housing starts for the same period.
U.S. Treasuries ended weaker, albeit off the day's price lows, eroding some of the gains made after Tuesday's weaker than expected CPI report.

Spreads to the U.S. continued to narrow with the long end differential having now been eroded by some 15 basis points since last Friday's close. Canadian bonds also outperformed the U.S., supported a solid performance in its currency in the face of the strong U.S. data.
